message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today National Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) and earned four NBA Most Valuable Player awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013). Known for his versatility—capable of playing point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward, and center—he combines size, athleticism, court vision, and basketball IQ.

Beyond the court, LeBron is a philanthropist, entrepreneur, and media personality. He founded the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the I PROMISE School, a public school for at‑risk children in Akron. He also launched the media company SpringHill Entertainment, producing films and television series, and has been involved in various endorsement deals with major brands. LeBron’s influence extends into social activism, particularly around issues of racial justice and education reform.
